main_text.p: giant, si qua spes affulgeat minimè frivola, posse se eam aliquâ saltem ex parte tueri. Quod in primis videre est in liberis civitatibus: quæ saevissimis bellorum tempe-statibus jactatæ, extrema subire pericula, & gravissimas tolerare obsidiones maluerunt, quàm libertate privari.

3492. Testantur hoc ATHENÆ, nequicquam bis à Xerxe & 3493. Mardonio captæ atque incensæ, teste Herodoto lib.7. & 8. iterumque bello Peloponnesiaco à Lysandro Lacedæmonio muris nudatæ, ut Xenophon scribit lib.2. 3584. ROMA in ipsâ adolescentiâ à Gallis Senonibus, duce Brenno direpta & incensa; indeque omnium gentium victrix, diuque rerum potita, quinquies à barbaris na-410.455. tionibus, Gothis, Vandalis, Herulis capta, cædibusque 472.476. direptione & incendiis deformata: HAMBURGUM, ob Christi nomen sexies ab impiis, Vandalis præsertim, cladem passum: de quo vide Cranzium lib.7. Metropol. 546. cap.1. & 5. MEDIOLANUM, à Friderico I. Imp. fame ad deditionem coactum, teste Sigonio lib.13. regni Italici: 1162. BYZANTIUM à Saracenis integro triennio terrâ marique frustrà obsessum: RHODUS insula, à Mahometé Turcarum Imp. terribili armorum apparatu terrâ marique per tres ferè menses incassum oppugnata, ac mille & trecentis bombardarum ictibus concussa: ut ex 718. Jovio refert Sabellici supplementum lib.9. & aliæ urbes quàm plurimæ. 1479. Quæ omnia evidenter probant; quantæ difficultatis res sit, liberæ civitati, etiam mediocriter potenti, bellum inferre: nisi forte aut seditio-ne plebeiâ, aut optimatum factionibus, aut alio intestino malo ea laboret. Sic nimirum pugnantibus contra Aristobulum Regem intestinâ seditione fratribus germanis, & gentem Judæorum in diversa studia trahentibus, supervenit Cn. Pompejus dux Romani exercitus: & HIEROSOLYMA captâ, Judæorum gentem tributariam fecit. Sic & GRÆCIÆ urbes florentissimas sub Macedonum servitutem discordia redegit: & validissimæ[?] nationi imposuit regnum Macedonicum ignobile. Sic & FLORENTINIS bello à Pontifice Julio II, Maximiliano I. Cæsare, & Aragoniæ Rege Fer-
Liberæ ci-vitates, ma-lo intestino laborantes, opprimi pos-sunt[?]

page.notes: The left margin holds the reference numbers 3492, 3493, 3584, 410.455, 472.476, 546, 1162, 718, 1479, 3908 and 3909; 3908 and 3909 are placed beside the Sic nimirum and exercitus lines, as their position in the scan is approximate. The margin note on liberae civitates is a multi-line note; its last word is partly cut off in the scan and is doubtful. The word beginning validissimae is cut at the edge of the scan and is doubtful. Paragraph division between "Testantur" and "Quae omnia" is uncertain: the scan shows no clear indent, so the text is kept as one paragraph. Long s is rendered as s throughout; the printed "f" forms in the scan are long s.
